about: What a CeaseNet gate must decide, in any language. Each case in `decide` runs the rules on `input`, and states the agent's own mode and the verdict for one call to the tool hashed `ask`. Each case in `covers` states whether a recall covers a file. Block numbers are strings. See arkiv/schema.md.

decide.why: No recall, so the call goes ahead.
A STOP signed by the owner on this tool's exact hash blocks the tool. The rest of the agent keeps working.
A STOP on one tool says nothing about another.
Anyone can write a record. A STOP from a key the owner did not sign with changes nothing.
Aiming straight at the agent does not help a stranger.
An owner's STOP on the agent's identity stops every tool it has.
An owner's STOP on the fleet stops all of that owner's agents.
An owner's STOP on the team stops the agents of that team.
A model is part of the agent itself, so a STOP on it stops the whole agent.
Addresses compare in lowercase. The same key written in capitals is the same key.
The key that issued a STOP can take it back.
A lift from anyone else is ignored, so nobody can undo an owner's STOP.
Only where an older trust list names a regulator can another key lift a STOP.
A lift counts only for the recall it names.
Publishing a fix says what to move to. The old version stays blocked.
A STOP can name a package and a version range.
A version outside the range is not covered.
A tool the gate was not told about is never let through.
With the list out of reach, an agent keeps working through the grace period.
After the grace period, each call needs a person.
After both periods, it fails closed.
Losing the internet never brings back what was stopped.
A normal recall is written by the verifier, not the owner. However many votes it has, it binds nobody until the owner approves it with a STOP.
The owner's approval is an ordinary STOP from the owner, so it binds at once.
Where the verifier is one this gate listens to, a warning with enough votes makes each call need a person.
Below the threshold it changes nothing.
One person voting three times counts once.
Votes count only while they outnumber votes against.
Only the verifier's own records count as votes.
A vote from outside the window is not counted, whatever its expiry says.
A regulator's dismissal ends a warning.
A warning that needed a person when the list was last readable still does.

covers.why: The exact hash covers the file.
A range on another package does not apply.
The upper bound itself is outside.
Caret stops at the next major.
Below 1.0.0, caret keeps the minor version.
Tilde stops at the next minor.
An x-range that does not match.
A prerelease is not covered by a plain range.
It is covered when the range names a prerelease of the same version.
A range that cannot be read covers nothing, so a badly written recall cannot stop what it did not name.
A version that cannot be read is not covered by a range.
